subject: Order form — commit ladder, invoicing cadence & tax evidence for legal review
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@northbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — commit ladder, invoicing cadence & tax evidence for legal review

Elena / Northbridge team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is our latest Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v2025-08-12.pdf) and a short Excel that maps the commit ladder and proposed invoicing cadence (Commit_Ladder_Proposal.xlsx). The key commercial asks we discussed:

- Minimum commit ladder: year 1 = USD 250k (50% upfront, 25% at month 6, 25% at month 12)
- Year 2 option: 15% uplift on committed units if exercised within 60 days
- Net terms: standard Net 30; Northbridge requested Net 45 — noted in the draft as an optional clause
- Taxes: Redwood needs W-9 (US) or VAT evidence for EU entities; I asked procurement to send tax docs

Kimberly / Legal: can you confirm if we can accept Net 45 for a 12-month term with an escrow-style upfront? Also flag any MSA cross-refs we should update for the commit ladder (section 3.2/3.4).

Ben / Sales: suggest we prepare a short rationale for the split invoicing cadence so procurement understands cashflow impact.

Elena, could you confirm the purchasing entity (legal name + tax ID) so we can populate the Order Form? If Northbridge can provide the W-9 by EOD Thursday that would keep DocuSign timing on track.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal legal check (Kimberly) on Net 45 + escrow language by Thu 14 Aug EOD
2) Procurement to share tax evidence and PO routing (Elena) by Thu 14 Aug
3) Rafael to circulate revised Order Form with DocuSign link by Fri 15 Aug

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2025-08-12.pdf (order form draft)
Attachment: Commit_Ladder_Proposal.xlsx (pricing schedule)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@northbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — commit ladder, invoicing cadence & tax evidence for legal review

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the materials. Quick read — a few items I want to flag for legal redline:

1) Net 45: we can accept Net 45 for customers with prior credit references, but the Order Form needs an explicit invoice schedule tied to the commit ladder (so payments are reconciled to committed tranches). Recommend adding wording: "Invoices due Net 45 from invoice date; payments not received within 60 days may trigger suspension of service for amounts outstanding against upcoming tranches."

2) Upfront/escrow language: if we take >30% upfront we should define refund/cancellation mechanics and tie the MSA Service Credits section to tranche-level deliverables.

3) Taxes: we will need Northbridge's tax residency evidence. For US entities W-9 is sufficient; for EU entities need VAT registration and country-specific invoicing address.

4) PO routing / entity: make sure the Order Form has a checkbox for "Billing entity same as purchasing entity" and capture AP contact info. If Northbridge wants invoices sent to a different entity, we need approval from finance.

Ben — can you prepare a one-pager (2 bullets max) that explains why the split invoicing protects both sides? I'll include that language so procurement sees the intent.

I'll aim to return redlines to Rafael by Thu 14 Aug 5pm PT.

Kimberly Park
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Runch time thoughts —

Short version for procurement: the proposed ladder smooths their cashflow while providing us the revenue visibility to reserve dedicated capacity. Key bullets we can put into an email to procurement:

- Tranche 1 (50%) secures onboarding & reserved pool; invoiced at contract signature; Net 45
- Tranche 2 (25%) covers mid-year usage ramp; invoiced at month 6
- Tranche 3 (25%) final settlement at month 12 or upon exercise of Year 2 option

If Northbridge needs Net 45 we can accept it but ask for the PO number on signature and the W-9 to be included by AP. If their AP requires Net 60 we need a finance escalation (not preferred).

I'll craft the two-line rationale and attach the Excel with an added column showing cashflow timing vs our burn assumptions.

-Ben

Kimberly sent redlines earlier today; I incorporated the Net 45 wording and added a short Annex A that defines the two onboarding milestones for the first tranche: (1) sandbox provisioning and (2) completion of initial data ingestion validation. Refund mechanics tied to those milestones are in Section 4.3 of the attached redline.

I've uploaded the revised Order Form to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcd-ordform-sign — you should see the envelope with the PO and W-9 attached. Please sign the Order Form and add the PO number on the signature page so our finance team can route invoices correctly.
